identity.title: Temperature Structures of Embedded Disks: Young Disks in Taurus Are Warm

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper we present ALMA observations of C$^{17}$O toward five young disks in Taurus to address the questions whether young disks are generally too warm for CO freeze-out and whether there is significant CO processing.

question.value: Are young disks too warm for CO freeze-out, and is there significant CO processing?

evidence.quote: A 3$\sigma$ column density upper limit of $\sim$ $8\times10^{13}$ cm$^{-2}$ is then found for HDO.

why_this_method.value: Use position-velocity structure and visibility models to distinguish disk emission from envelope contamination

evidence.quote: In these diagrams, disk emission is located at small angular offsets and high velocities, while envelope emission extends to larger offsets but has lower velocities.

A first assessment of the envelope contribution to the line emission can be made by comparing generic models of either only a Keplerian disk or a disk embedded in an envelope to the observed visibility amplitudes.

referee_caveats_inferred: Snowline radii are morphology-based estimates without formal uncertainty distributions.
Using a shared L1527 model family limits source-specific interpretation of other disks.
The supplied prose H2CO column-density range disagrees with the detailed table; answer keys should distinguish the two.
The tabulated TMC1-W H2CO abundance appears inconsistent with its C17O/H2CO and C17O/H2 ratios; preserve the printed value pending clarification.
The limited sample and heterogeneous literature comparison do not independently establish a universal evolutionary sequence.
